title: Prefetch shared aggregates and stable cursors for Console dashboard queries
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Several console dashboard endpoints that surface usage analytics (tokens per route, active tenants, top-models, per-token cost over time) have erratic P95 latency spikes and cause high DB load during peak queries. Current cursor-based pagination is brittle when we rebuild or reindex analytic tables, and many dashboard widgets execute overlapping aggregations that repeat work across requests.

Goal: Reduce read latency and backend DB CPU by introducing a small set of tenant-aware materialized aggregates + a shared prefetch cache layer, and make cursor tokens stable across index rebuilds using snapshot-based sequence anchors. Provide fallback to live queries for very fresh data. Maintain strong consistency guarantees for owner-facing dashboards (<=30s eventual consistency) and avoid long maintenance windows during schema changes.
acceptance_criteria: P95 API latency for target dashboard routes decreases by >=40% under synthetic load compared to baseline
Average number of DB rows scanned per dashboard call reduces by >=60%
Cursor pagination tokens remain valid after index rebuilds or MV refresh (no 500s or 400s due to invalid cursor) during canary window
Cache hit ratio for shared prefetch layer >=70% for top-50 tenants during peak
Safe rollback path: health checks will cut traffic to old query path without data loss
technical_notes: Introduce two new per-tenant materialized tables: tenant_daily_usage_agg (partitioned by date) and tenant_top_routes_mv (top-k routes weekly). Both are lightweight summaries with approximate counters for cost and token counts.

Create a small in-process shared prefetch service (Go) inside console-backend that precomputes the required aggregate tiles for a requested dashboard route and populates an LRU-backed memory cache keyed by (tenant_id, tile_type, date_range, snapshot_id). TTLs: 30s for near-real-time tiles, 10m for weekly top-k.

Stable cursor design: cursor token = base64(JSON) with fields {snapshot_id, sequenced_range_start, sequenced_range_end, anchor_time}. snapshot_id is the timestamp of the MV snapshot or a monotonically increasing logical generation id from MV refresh job. On index rebuild, snapshot_id changes but cursors referencing an older snapshot remain readable by translating sequenced offsets using a translation table kept for 24h.

MV refresh strategy: incremental refresh jobs using insert/update into partitioned MV and write through a small journal table (mv_generation_journal) to record snapshot_id -> partition_end_time mapping. Refreshes scheduled every 15s for daily tiles and hourly for weekly top-k during peak; full rebuilds only in maintenance windows.

Query fallback: if prefetch cache miss or MV stale beyond defined freshness threshold, route to optimized live query path that uses new composite indexes (see migration DDL below). Live queries include LIMIT + seek-based pagination to avoid full scans.

DB changes: add composite index ON analytics.events (tenant_id, date, route_id, created_at) USING btree; create partitioning by range(date) for tenant_daily_usage_agg; add partial indexes for heavy tenants if needed.

Data correctness: MV uses deterministic aggregations (SUM, COUNT) and last-value for small metadata columns to ensure stable pagination ordering. Index rebuilds will not change ordering because order uses (snapshot_id, route_id, created_at).
Observability: Add new perf dashboards: MV refresh lag, cache hit ratio, prefetch QPS, DB rows scanned per query, request path breakdown (prefetch vs live).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement prefetch service and MV schema in staging. Add unit tests and local benchmarks (Feb 18–Feb 24).
Phase 1 (staging canary): Enable prefetch + MV for 5 internal tenants and run 48h of query load tests. Monitor latency and DB load (Feb 25–Mar 3).
Phase 2 (prod limited): Canary to 10% of tenant traffic for non-critical dashboards; validate cursor stability across an index rebuild simulated in canary group (Mar 4–Mar 10).
Phase 3 (full roll): Gradually increase to 100% following success criteria and sweep for per-tenant corner cases; schedule full MV rebuild outside business hours (Mar 11–Mar 15).
Rollback: feature flag to turn off prefetch and route back to legacy queries; MV refresh journal preserved for safe rehydration.
testing_plan: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode and translation logic (including translation table expiry).
Integration test: simulate index rebuild while cursors are active and assert no 4xx/5xx for paginated calls.
Load test: k6 script that reproduces dashboard traffic pattern from top-50 tenants and measures p50/p95 with and without prefetch. Baseline derived from 2025-01-12 run.
A/B canary comparison using server-side feature flag to measure DB CPU, query counts, and cache hit ratio over 48h.
Chaos test: induce MV refresh job delays and ensure fallback to live queries does not cause excessive latency amplification (>2x expected).
metrics: mv.refresh_lag target: <=30s for daily tiles, <=10m for weekly top-k
error.rate for dashboard endpoints target: <0.1% (no increase during rollout)
